question: On 31 August 2026, the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights called on Ecuador to ensure pluralism in the 29 November elections and to prevent arbitrary exclusion. The suspension of Revolución Ciudadana for nine months, followed by the suspension of the AMIGO movement, which was due to field its candidates, is clearly intended to prevent the main opposition force from taking part in the elections.

These decisions raise serious concerns about pluralism, freedom of association, political rights and the free choice of voters. They demonstrate an instrumental use of institutions to exclude a political opponent.

In her answer of 30 April 2026 to question E-000978/20261, the Vice-President/High Representative focused on dialogue and cooperation, despite European warnings about disproportionate restrictions on political rights. Faced with this deterioration in the rule of law, the European Union must take concrete action. Will the Vice-President/High Representative: 1.
state what verifiable measures the EU has taken since 30 April 2026?
condemn the suspension of Revolución Ciudadana and demand that it be allowed to take part in future elections?

support the suspension of Ecuador from the EU-Colombia-Peru trade agreement, to which Ecuador acceded in 2017, for as long as Article 1 of the agreement, on democratic principles, human rights and the rule of law, is not respected?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.11.2026) The High Representative/Vice-President and the European External Action Service are following closely the latest developments related to the situation of human rights, democracy and the rule of law in Ecuador.

This includes the nine-month suspension of the Revolución Ciudadana political movement, as stated in the reply to written question E-000978/2026 on 30 April 20261, and the broader context of the upcoming local elections, scheduled for the end of November 2026.

In its monitoring of the situation, the EU uses inter alia the findings, reports, and rulings of independent international and regional human rights mechanisms such as UN bodies and the Inter-American Commission on Human Rights.

Respect for democratic principles, human rights, and the rule of law constitutes an essential element of relations between the EU and Ecuador, including the Trade Agreement between the EU and its Member States, and Colombia, Peru, and Ecuador2, as stated in the replies to written questions E-002818/2026 on 21 August 20263 and E-000978/2026 on 30 April 2026.

The suspension of a party from the Agreement, while possible in case of violations of its essential elements clause, remains a last resort measure. The EU’s preference is still to engage in dialogue at this stage, since partial or full suspension of an agreement may have significant detrimental effects on the population of the partner country, including those in a vulnerable situation.

As a result, the EU has been continuously raising its concerns directly and regularly with the Government of Ecuador, at all levels and through multiple channels. These include the EUEcuador High-Level Political Dialogue and the Human Rights Dialogue, both taking place on an annual basis.
